newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to decide on companies for privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Israel to decide on companies for privatisation.

text.p: Israeli cabinet ministers will consider on Monday what government-owned companies to sell under a wide-ranging privatisation plan, a spokesman for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Sunday.
It will be the first time the ministerial committee on privatisation will examine a sell-off list recently drafted by officials in the prime minister's office.
"The list will be brought to the ministerial committee tomorrow (Monday) but they will not vote on it," Netanyahu's spokesman said.
Government sources said the document named companies but did not spell out how each would be sold.
Among the companies slated for sale this year are Bezeq Israel Telecom, Zim Israel Navigation Shipping and Israel Chemicals Ltd, government sources said.
Officials in the government have said Israel would favour selling shares whenever possible on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.

The ministerial committee will examine a list of companies slated for privatisation this year, another list of companies to be sold in 1998-99 and a third roster of firms to be privatised at a later period, government sources said.
The committee on privatisation comprises Netanyahu, Finance Minister Dan Meridor and Justice Minister Tzahi Hanegbi.

Netanyahu, elected last May, has promised to sell off most government-owned companies. He said in November that he hoped to raise more than $1 billion worth of assets through privatisation by the end of 1997.
Market sources say the privatisation programme is expected to be greeted favourably in foreign markets but investors have said Netanyahu's targets for raising money may be unrealistic.
